## Projects
### GrantLens — Research Funding Discovery
Category: Research Discovery AI
An evidence-grounded research assistant for hybrid grant discovery, applicant-fit checks, literature reviews, cited document Q&A and deadline tracking.
README overview: Hybrid semantic search over research funding, plus an academic research assistant. Watch the 8-minute demo : every feature, the stack and models, and the measured results, including what didn't work.
Verified features:
- Search: Keyword (BM25) and meaning (embedding) search fused into one ranking, with filters for status, agency, close date and amount
- Fit check: Compares your profile with a grant's own text. Every met or not-met verdict must quote the grant, or it is downgraded to unclear
- Find grants for my work: Paste a summary or give an ORCID; get open grants ranked against your work, with your closest paper shown for each
- Paper search: Scholarly papers through OpenAlex
- Literature reviews: Themes, per-paper annotations and theme summaries, each backed by a quote from the abstract. Built as a background job
- Documents: Upload a PDF and ask questions; answers carry a verified citation, and unanswerable questions say so
- Watchlist, saved searches, deadlines: Track grants, email alerts and reminders (verified addresses only), a deadline calendar
Architecture: - Backend: Flask, Postgres 16 with pgvector (HNSW), Redis, a separate worker process for slow jobs - Frontend: Next.js 16 and TypeScript - Run and ship: Docker Compose, Caddy (automatic HTTPS), GitHub Actions (tests, images to GHCR, deploy script with rollback) - Models: BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 embeddings run locally; OpenAI gpt-4o-mini writes answers, summaries and checks. Llama 3.1 8B through Hugging Face is an optional backend ( LLM BACKEND=hf )
Technologies: Next.js 16, Flask, pgvector, Hybrid search
Page: https://vaibhavbansal.in/projects/grantlens-research-funding-discovery
Repository: https://github.com/VaibhavBansal26/grantlens
README: https://github.com/VaibhavBansal26/grantlens/blob/master/README.md

### MemoRank — Long-Horizon Agent Memory
Category: Agent Memory Research
MemoRank — Long-Horizon Agent Memory is a Agent Memory Research project by Vaibhav Bansal built with Python, MCP, OpenAI Agents SDK, Anthropic SDK, BM25, Dense Retrieval, Cross-encoder Reranking, SQLite, A/B Testing.
README overview: Long-horizon memory for security-investigation agents. No model training anywhere: retrieval (BM25 + dense), a pretrained cross-encoder, and entity-aware heuristics decide which records an agent sees. Served over MCP to OpenAI Agents SDK and Anthropic SDK agents. Includes an evaluation harness for LongMemEval and LoCoMo, a synthetic security-investigation set, CI gates, and a pre-registered online A/B.
Verified features:
- memorank
- Results at a glance
- Architecture
- Use as a library
- Problem
- Memory schema (fixed)
- Baselines
Architecture: flowchart LR A[Agent Anthropic SDK / OpenAI Agents SDK] -- MCP -- M[Memory server store memory, recall, rerank] A -- MCP -- L[Alert server live 2-day window] M -- P[dense + BM25 candidates cross-encoder score entity-scoped recency, entity chaining] F[Feature flag sticky hash, 50/50] -. picks variant .- M A -- T[(Session log SQLite)]
Technologies: Python, MCP, OpenAI Agents SDK, Anthropic SDK, BM25, Dense Retrieval, Cross-encoder Reranking, SQLite, A/B Testing
Page: https://vaibhavbansal.in/projects/memorank-long-horizon-agent-memory
Repository: https://github.com/VaibhavBansal26/memorank
README: https://github.com/VaibhavBansal26/memorank/blob/main/README.md

### AI-Powered Self-Healing Data Pipeline
Category: AI Data Reliability
AI-Powered Self-Healing Data Pipeline is a AI Data Reliability project by Vaibhav Bansal built with FastAPI, React, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Redis, Airflow, Docker, LangGraph, RAG Incident Memory, MCP Tools.
README overview: A production-style reliability lab for streaming data pipelines. The platform combines FastAPI, React, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Redis, Apache Airflow, Docker, LangGraph, RAG incident memory and MCP-style operational tools to demonstrate record repair, stage monitoring, safe automated recovery, human approval and recovery observability. Project status: Portfolio/research demo, not a hardened production deployment. Recovery actions can affect local Docker services; use in an isolated development environment.
Verified features:
- Ingestion and data repair: Validates Kafka events, applies deterministic rules, optionally reasons about harder problems with an LLM, persists valid records, and routes unrecoverable events to the DLQ.
- Infrastructure recovery: Monitors Docker-backed services, detects stopped consumers and unavailable dependencies, invokes an allowlisted recovery action and verifies the result.
- Safe autonomy: A background auto-healer monitors the system; the recovery policy/agent selects allowed actions; risky operations require human review.
- AI operations: Incident memory / RAG, traces, tool-call evaluation, semantic caching, cost summaries and an agent activity timeline.
- Control room: React pages for the live pipeline map, background console, approvals, incidents, replay, metrics and AI engineering.
Architecture: A production-style reliability lab for streaming data pipelines. The platform combines FastAPI, React, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Redis, Apache Airflow, Docker, LangGraph, RAG incident memory and MCP-style operational tools to demonstrate record repair, stage monitoring, safe automated recovery, human approval and recovery observability. Project status: Portfolio/research demo, not a hardened production deployment. Recovery actions can affect local Docker services; use in an isolated development environment.
Technologies: FastAPI, React, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Redis, Airflow, Docker, LangGraph, RAG Incident Memory, MCP Tools
Page: https://vaibhavbansal.in/projects/ai-powered-self-healing-data-pipeline
Repository: https://github.com/VaibhavBansal26/Self-Healing-Data-Pipeline
README: https://github.com/VaibhavBansal26/Self-Healing-Data-Pipeline/blob/main/README.md

- Admin
- Ads
- Ai
- Analyticsapi
- Assets
- Auth
- Billing
Architecture: Funnels is one Node process (Hono on SQLite by default, or PostgreSQL) that serves the JSON API, the built React app, published funnel pages (by Host header and on built-in /s/... addresses) and signed previews. An in-process worker drains a database-backed job queue. Funnels can also be published as static sites to Cloudflare Pages, and an optional Cloudflare Worker can sit in front. The code map, jobs, route groups and the full data model are in FUNCTIONS.md.

### Friday AI Assistant
Category: Agentic AI
A privacy-conscious macOS assistant combining realtime voice, local memory and approval-gated actions across coding and communication tools.
README overview: Friday is a privacy-conscious desktop AI assistant for macOS. It combines a React/Tauri desktop interface with a local FastAPI service, realtime voice, approval-gated external actions, coding tools, communications, content workflows, learning tools, and local memory foundations. Friday is designed to show evidence for completed actions. High-impact operations such as sending email, publishing content, creating repositories, pushing Git commits, or submitting forms require explicit approval.
Verified features:
- Voice and conversation: Realtime speech, transcription, spoken responses, tool routing, startup greeting — OpenAI API key, microphone permission
- Tasks and planning: Create and manage tasks, learning topics, study plans, ideas, and notifications — None for local/in-memory use
- Gmail: Connect Gmail, sync recent messages, summarize mail, create visible drafts, and send after approval — Google OAuth client and Gmail API
- Spotify: Open Spotify, search for a track, select a Spotify Connect device, and play music — Spotify Premium and Spotify OAuth app
- GitHub and coding: List and clone repositories, inspect trees, read/create/edit files, open Finder or VS Code, run safe commands, create repositories, commit/push with approval — GitHub CLI authentication; VS Code CLI for editor actions
- LinkedIn content: Create copyable drafts, preview publishing, and publish through an approved connected application — LinkedIn developer application and approved products/scopes
- Content studio: Draft LinkedIn, Medium, X, Instagram, and other channel content in visible workspaces — Publishing credentials vary by provider
Architecture: Trust boundaries: UI is untrusted input; FastAPI authenticates a local session; supervisor output is advisory; policy and verification are deterministic; adapters alone resolve credential references; external content is inert data; PostgreSQL is authoritative for confirmed facts and workflow state.
Technologies: Tauri, React, FastAPI, Realtime AI
Page: https://vaibhavbansal.in/projects/friday-ai-assistant
Repository: https://github.com/VaibhavBansal26/friday-ai-assistant

### FidelityMem — Adaptive Hybrid Memory
Category: AI Research
A recall-constrained hybrid memory layer that controls active context, long-term storage, compression and evidence restoration for LLM agents.
README overview: Module Role --- --- window.py Adaptive working window: per-message retention score, boundary triggers (token pressure, topic shift, task completion, inactivity), eviction into extraction. extraction.py Candidate memories with types (semantic / episodic / procedural / relational), entities, numbers, dates, negations, relations. validation.py Stage 1 source & consistency (trust, contradiction, supersede-not-delete, untrusted-instruction guard). Stage 2 relevance & utility (durability score, fact-aware dedupe). compression.py Four-level compression ladder and the fidelity gate : probes built from the raw source must survive, or the level backs off. Stage 3. stores/ Immutable archival store (JSONL-persistable), BM25, dense index with a hermetic hashing embedder, relation graph with relation-following expansion and hub penalty, trie for exact/prefix identifiers. retrieval/ Query classification, per-type plans, RRF fusion + ranking function, relation chaining for multi-hop, sufficiency check and raw-source expansion, token-budgeted context. controller.py Recall-constrained policy search over (compression level, top-k, expansion budget, routes) with tuning/hold-out split, promotion, rejec
Verified features:
- FidelityMem
- What is in the box
- Benchmark
- LLM-judged evaluation (Phase 6)
- needs ANTHROPIC API KEY (or ANTHROPIC AUTH TOKEN / ant auth login )
- plumbing check without a credential
- Status
Architecture: The implementation is centered on Python, LLM Agents, Hybrid Retrieval, BM25, RRF. The repository is organized into docs, fidelitymem, scripts areas. Delivery and dependency evidence includes Python project manifest.
Technologies: Python, Hybrid retrieval, BM25, RRF
Page: https://vaibhavbansal.in/projects/fidelitymem-adaptive-hybrid-memory
Repository: https://github.com/VaibhavBansal26/FidelityMem
README: https://github.com/VaibhavBansal26/FidelityMem/blob/claude/compassionate-clarke-bpch7h/README.md

### Ridehail — Realtime Mobility Platform
Category: Mobility Platform
A production-shaped ride-sharing system with live dispatch, dynamic fares, customer and rider apps, operations tooling and balanced payment ledgers.
README overview: Part Where What --- --- --- API src/ Spring Boot 3, JPA, Flyway on Postgres, JWT roles CUSTOMER / RIDER / ADMIN , STOMP WebSocket Admin panel admin-web/ Next.js: live map, trips, riders, payments, ledger, disputes, incidents, support, rider verification, audit log (docs/ADMIN PANEL.md) Rider and customer web apps clients/apps/rider-web , customer-web Next.js, with maps (Leaflet), road routes, address search, vehicle pictures and live car tracking; sign-in cookies are held by the app's server, never by browser JavaScript Phone apps clients/apps/rider-mobile , customer-mobile Expo / React Native, tokens in the keychain, with the same maps, routes, address search and vehicle pictures (the map is a Leaflet page in a WebView: no native map library or key). Tested and bundled, but not yet run on a device Shared client clients/packages/api Typed REST and realtime client with schema-checked responses (clients/README.md)
Verified features:
- Dynamic fares: upfront quotes with demand and supply surge pricing, locked at booking.
- Dispatch: nearest-rider offers with timeouts; the rider accepts or declines. Live rider location for the customer.
- Maps, routes and live tracking: the customer searches for a destination by name, sees the pickup, destination and the road between them on a map, and watches the driver's vehicle (a bike, auto, sedan or SUV) move live; the driver sees every offer, and the trip, on a map. Several requests at once stack on the driver's screen, each on its own map. The admin map shows every driver as their vehicle. Search and routes go through the API (docs/GEO.md); tiles come from OpenStreetMap by default ( MAP TILE URL changes that).
- Realtime: offers, trip updates and rider location over WebSocket. One instance out of the box; many with RabbitMQ and Redis (docs/SCALING.md, docs/LIVE LOCATION.md).
- Payments: the card is charged when a trip ends; a double-entry ledger that must balance (enforced in the database); commission; refunds.
- Rider payouts: riders withdraw their share through Stripe Connect (Accounts v2, Express dashboard). A payout waits for the provider's settled funds rather than failing.
- Disputes and provider problems: chargebacks are recorded and the rider's share frozen until decided; text evidence is compiled and submitted from the admin panel; failed bank payouts, reversed transfers and failed refunds become incidents for a person (docs/DISPUTES.md).
Architecture: The implementation is centered on Java, Java 21, Spring Boot 3, PostgreSQL, Next.js. The repository is organized into admin-web, clients, docker, docs, scripts, src areas. Delivery and dependency evidence includes Docker, Docker Compose, Node package manifest, Maven.
Technologies: Spring Boot 3, Next.js, WebSockets, Stripe Connect
Page: https://vaibhavbansal.in/projects/ridehail-realtime-mobility-platform
Repository: https://github.com/VaibhavBansal26/ridehail-platform
README: https://github.com/VaibhavBansal26/ridehail-platform/blob/main/README.md

### Health Semantic Search — Cited Medical Retrieval
Category: Health AI
A self-hostable search system over public health documents with access-aware retrieval, hybrid ranking, source citations and refusal when evidence is insufficient.
README overview: Permission-aware, cited semantic search over public health documents. Built stage by stage, with every design decision and measurement logged. The goal is a product a health system could adopt: self-hostable, answers always cite their source, and "no supported answer" beats a guess. Live app: https://health-semantic-search.onrender.com (free tier: it sleeps when idle, so the first load can take a minute; search only, no cited answers, see below) Research write-up: docs/PAPER.md, a workshop-style draft with every number traced to ENGINEERING LOG.md Full app with cited answers: https://huggingface.co/spaces/Vaibhavbansal26/health-semantic-search-app (same React app, reranker and cited answers; free CPU, so answers take 3-6 s) Original Gradio demo: the Space Vaibhavbansal26/health-semantic-search (reranker, no accounts)

- Health Semantic Search
- What it is
- Stack
- Status
- Results so far
- Architecture
- Data
Architecture: Layer Choice Notes --- --- --- Front end React 18, Vite 5, plain CSS about 52 kB gzipped; served by the API process, no separate host API FastAPI, uvicorn search, accounts, admin; security headers, per-request access mask Accounts and tokens SQLite, scrypt, PyJWT (RS256) one-hour tokens with a jti , sign-out and admin revocation, login rate limit Keyword search bm25s with a Snowball stemmer index built once, loaded memory-mapped Dense search BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 PyTorch in the full engine, ONNX Runtime (fastembed) in the lite one Fusion and routing weighted reciprocal rank fusion, identifier router NDC, CAS and imprint queries go to keyword search only Reranker and answers bge-reranker-base, extractive answers with a refusal threshold full engine only (about 2 GB) Access control boolean mask inside every retriever, mask-keyed cache document, tenant and section rules Corpus, sync Postgres 16 + pgvector, DailyMed, openFDA, ClinicalTrials.gov connectors kill-safe incremental sync, versioned index publishing Evaluation recall@k, MRR, nDCG, paired bootstrap five model-written question sets, tooling for a real-query set Packaging Docker (multi-stage), Render Blueprint ( render.yaml ) image about 700 MB; runs in under 250 MB of RAM CI GitHub Actions pytest on Python 3.11 and 3.13 (PR 15) Two engines share one API. The full engine ( HSS ENGINE=full ) has the reranker and cited answers and needs about 2 GB. The lite engine ( hss.lite , the default) fits 512 MB: chunk text in SQLite, memory-mapped BM25 and float16 vectors, an ONNX query encoder. On 60 questions it returned the same
Technologies: FastAPI, Hybrid retrieval, BGE embeddings, pgvector

### Heart Disease Prediction using Generative AI, Streamlit, OpenAI
Category: Machine Learning
An interactive health-risk prediction workflow combining a trained machine-learning model with Streamlit and generative AI guidance.
README overview: Heart-risk estimate + personalised next steps from a hybrid content / collaborative recommender.
Verified features:
- Risk model — predicts a heart-disease risk score from 11 clinical inputs. Candidates (each in one sklearn Pipeline , imputation fitted inside CV folds): logistic regression, gradient boosting and a PyTorch MLP .
- Hybrid recommender — ranks 13 lifestyle / screening / clinical interventions:
- Content-based: patient needs (lipids, BP, glucose, fitness, metabolic, cardiac work-up) matched to each intervention's target vector.
- Collaborative: a PyTorch two-tower model. The patient tower is an MLP on features plus the mean embedding of interventions the patient already liked; the item tower is an id embedding plus content features. It handles cold start (features only) and warm start (liked items).
- Hybrid: α·content + (1-α)·collaborative , with α tuned on a validation split. A safety rule always surfaces a cardiology referral at high scores.
- Education links from the NIH/NLM MedlinePlus web service (free, no key).
- MLflow experiment tracking and model registry, browsable from the app's 🧪 MLflow tab.
Architecture: The implementation is centered on Python, Generative AI, Streamlit, Machine Learning, Docker. The repository is organized into artifacts, data, deploy, docs, medapp, reports areas. Delivery and dependency evidence includes Docker, Docker Compose, Python requirements.
Technologies: Streamlit, Machine Learning, OpenAI, Docker
Page: https://vaibhavbansal.in/projects/heart-disease-prediction-using-generative-ai-streamlit-openai
Repository: https://github.com/VaibhavBansal26/medical-app
README: https://github.com/VaibhavBansal26/medical-app/blob/main/README.md

### Grapesjs Advance Components
Category: Package & Extension
Grapesjs Advance Components is a Package & Extension project by Vaibhav Bansal built with Npm package using react js , grapesjs.
README overview: - promptsite , a command line tool. It writes a multi-page site from one sentence with your own model, lets you polish it in a visual editor, audits it for leaked secrets , and deploys it to Cloudflare Pages or Netlify. - grapesjs-advance-components , a GrapesJS plugin with 41 accessible, themeable blocks (pricing, testimonials, team, tabs, forms that submit, Stripe checkout and more), defineComponent for your own blocks, and multi-page export. ### Natural Disaster Prediction & Management 
Category: Machine Learning
Natural Disaster Prediction & Management  is a Machine Learning project by Vaibhav Bansal built with Python, Flask, Google API,Machine Learning Algorithms, Deep Learning Methods.
README overview: Estimates, live data and alerting for earthquakes, tsunamis, floods, hurricanes and storms. Started as a VIT University capstone in 2020 (Flask 1, TensorFlow 1) and rebuilt in 2026 on FastAPI, scikit-learn, HTMX, Tailwind and Leaflet, with live feeds and a Claude-powered assistant. Outputs are statistical estimates and other organisations' live data. They are not operational forecasts or warnings. Earthquakes cannot be predicted: the earthquake page reports a historical hazard rate, and real-time alerts come from the USGS feed, not from a model.
Verified features:
- Home: A live 3D globe of this week's USGS earthquakes, with module cards
- Earthquake: Historical hazard for any place (rate and probability of M 6, 7, 8), the live USGS map, the week's strongest real earthquakes with one-click "Nearby help"
- Flood: River level 1, 3 and 6 hours ahead for one gauge, shown next to "no change"
- Tsunami, Hurricane, Storm: Small models with their held-out skill shown on the page
- Live: GDACS global alerts, a weather outlook for any place, and the real-event alert watcher
- Assistant: Plain-language questions answered with live tools and cited guidance (Claude key needed)
- Alerts: Hospitals and police near a place or epicentre, then alert your contacts by email or SMS, optionally in other languages
Architecture: This is the short map. Detail lives in code-walkthrough.md (backend), frontend.md (browser side), models.md (every model) and statistics.md (generated numbers). A FastAPI application that renders server-side Jinja2 pages, enhanced with HTMX. Models are trained once from the command line and loaded from disk at request time. Nothing trains, downloads or writes files inside a web request.
Technologies: Python, Flask, Google API, Machine Learning Algorithms, Deep Learning Methods
Page: https://vaibhavbansal.in/projects/natural-disaster-prediction-and-management
Repository: https://github.com/VaibhavBansal26/Capstone-2020-Natural-Disaster-Prediction
README: https://github.com/VaibhavBansal26/Natural-Disaster-Prediction/blob/master/README.md
